title: Orchestrator restarts a stuck replica via the liveness probe without external dependency coupling
asA: orchestrator running the deployed application under a supervising process (Kubernetes kubelet, systemd, or equivalent)
iWant: a liveness endpoint that answers pass or fail strictly on whether the process is running its event loop
soThat: I restart a wedged replica without letting a downstream dependency outage cascade into a restart storm across every replica

acceptanceCriteria.description: The application serves the liveness endpoint at a stable HTTP path supplied by project configuration under `probeInterface.paths.liveness` (with no shipped default from v2.0.0); a GET returns 200 when the process is running its event loop and returns application/json with a status field equal to pass. When observability-probe-endpoints v1.1.0 or later is composed on the same project the resolved profile liveness path substitutes for this configuration entry automatically.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the process is running normally with its event loop responsive
acceptanceCriteria.when: an unauthenticated GET is issued against the liveness path
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status code is 200, the response carries the header owned on TAC-801-observability-essentials-liveness-probe.responsibilities[1], and the JSON body's status field equals pass

acceptanceCriteria.description: The liveness probe handler evaluates entirely in-process; a probe hit issues zero network calls to any declared dependency, verifiable by observing the network egress from the probe path. Template values the applying agent sets: The applying agent sets the elicited declared-dependency-set; the AC substitutes the project's dependency names for the illustrative paymentsProvider / primaryStore tokens.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the process is running and a network-egress observer is attached to the probe path
acceptanceCriteria.when: a GET is issued against the liveness path
acceptanceCriteria.then: the observer records zero egress connections attributable to the probe handler between request receipt and response send

acceptanceCriteria.description: The liveness probe answer is independent of the readiness dependency set: pulling a declared readiness dependency offline never turns the liveness probe fail on its own.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the process is running and every declared readiness dependency is offline
acceptanceCriteria.when: a GET is issued against the liveness path
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status code is 200 and the JSON body's status field equals pass

acceptanceCriteria.description: When `probeInterface.paths.liveness` is absent from project configuration AND observability-probe-endpoints is not composed on the same project, the essentials blueprint refuses boot with a stable-coded error `PROBE_INTERFACE_PATHS_MISSING` naming the missing configuration key.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project applying essentials v2.0.0 alone with no probeInterface.paths.liveness in configuration
acceptanceCriteria.then: the boot fails with the stable-coded error PROBE_INTERFACE_PATHS_MISSING and the error message names probeInterface.paths.liveness as the missing key

acceptanceCriteria.description: A liveness handler on a process whose in-process self-check predicate returns fail (a scheduled watchdog tick that has not fired within its budget) answers HTTP 503 with content-length 0 and an empty body, so the orchestrator restarts the process on the next probe interval. The predicate is response-capable by design: it observes a boolean the handler reads without I/O. Template values the applying agent sets: The applying agent supplies the elicited liveness-probe-path and the project-owned self-check predicate; the AC substitutes both.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running application with an operator-declared watchdog tick scheduled every 1 second and a 5-second budget; the tick has not fired for 6 seconds so the predicate is fail
acceptanceCriteria.when: the orchestrator issues HTTP GET on the elicited liveness-probe-path
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is HTTP 503 with content-length 0 and an empty body; a follow-up GET while the predicate stays fail continues to answer 503; a GET after the predicate returns pass answers 200
